_readme: VAG #105 verifier meta-eval corpus. Each item is a FIXED implementation the adversarial reviewer judges against its title + acceptance_criteria (it reads the files, not a diff or the tests). label=bugged means the code contains a real defect the reviewer SHOULD refute; label=clean means it's correct and SHOULD survive. bug_class categorizes the defect. stub_verdict is what a PERFECT reviewer would return (refuted for bugged, survived for clean) — it drives the offline dry-run so the harness (scoring + gate + report) can be exercised with zero model calls; a real run replaces it with the actual reviewer's verdict and shows how far it falls short. Keep the corpus BALANCED (both classes) or the gate is meaningless. Deterministic stdlib-only Python so a defect is a genuine logic error, not an environment artifact.

items.title: Return the last N elements of a list
acceptance_criteria: last_n([1,2], 5) == [1,2] (n larger than list returns the whole list)
items.label: bugged
items.note: last_n([1,2,3,4],2) returns [2,3,4]-ish / wrong count; also n=0 -> xs[1:] not []
